candidates.title: Safe Drinking Water Facilities Information System for Pennsylvania 2018 - Current Environmental Protection
candidates.description: Safe Drinking Water Information System (SDWIS) is EPA’s national database that manages and collects public water system information from states, including reports of drinking water standard violations, reporting and monitoring violations, and other basic information. The data derived in the State of Pennsylvania is published and searchable online on the www.pa.gov website. This set contains the Water System Facility data, which will be updated annually for the prior calendar year in the first Quarter of the following year.

candidates.title: Safe Drinking Water Sample Results Information Systems Pennsylvania 2010 - Current Environmental Protection
candidates.description:
Pennsylvania collects and manages public drinking water system information in the Pennsylvania Drinking Water Information System (PADWIS).
The data includes water system inventory information, drinking water sample results for testing required by the regulations and violations of PA Safe Drinking Water Regulations, pertaining to monitoring/reporting requirements, MCL exceedances, and treatment techniques. Much of this data is searchable via the www.drinkingwater.state.pa.us website. This set contains drinking water sample results reported on behalf of Pennsylvania’s regulated public water supplies. The data is updated quarterly.

candidates.title: MS4 Regulated Areas Current Statewide Environmental
candidates.description:
MS4 Regulated Areas (BCW_MS4RegulatedAreas) Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection, Bureau of Clean Water, MS4 Regulated Areas. Areas that require NPDES MS4 permit coverage.

Municipalities and other entities, such as universities and prisons, that meet certain standards must obtain NPDES permit coverage for discharges of stormwater from their municipal separate storm sewer system (MS4s). The part of the municipality regulated by the permittee's MS4 permit is the portion of the municipality designated by the 2010 Census as urbanized area, plus any additional areas designated by the 2020 Census as urban areas with a population of 50,000 or more. This shapefile shows the area regulated by MS4 permits throughout the state.

This dataset was created using two shapefiles from the Census Bureau. The census data is a snapshot in time. When data from the 2030 Census becomes available a new dataset will be created.

candidates.title: Lake Erie Coastal Zone Aerial Imagery & Delaware Estuary Coastal Zone Imagery Environmental Protection
candidates.description:
Multiple datasets: Lake Erie Coastal Zone Aerial Imagery 1984, 1986, 1998-2017 & Delaware Estuary Coastal Zone Imagery 1986, 1989-2017 Environmental Protection

The Coastal Resources Management Program within the PA Department of Environmental Protection funded 30 years of annual aerial photography acquisition of the by the PA Department of Transportation.  

This included portions of the Lake Erie Coastal Zone (within Erie County) and the Delaware Estuary Coastal Zone (within Delaware, Bucks, and Philadelphia Counties).  Data products include scanned film in TIFF and JPEG formats in vertical near-infrared (later replaced by natural color) at alternating high- and low-altitude scales, in addition to selected years of “oblique” aerial photography, where images are captured at an angled (non-vertical) perspective.

The imagery datasets are currently available publicly through this link and as open data via the Pennsylvania Spatial Data Access (PASDA) at https://data.pa.gov/d/75nz-5f7x
 
Datasets were partially funded through a federal coastal zone management grant provided by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), United States Department of Commerce, under multiple annual awards. Adopted in 2011, the Data Sharing Directive for NOAA Grants, Cooperative Agreements, and Contracts, requires that environmental data funded by NOAA be made publicly accessible.

Here is a link to the NOAA Data Management Handbook: https://www.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/2025-03/N
